title: Harness profile
description: How Aboard works with one harness: how to check it, start it, run it headless, resume it, give it an identity and deliver messages into its sessions. One file per harness, at adapters/<harness>/profile.yaml. aboard init, the delivery daemon, aboard doctor and the launchers read it. Command lines are argument vectors, never shell strings; {prompt}, {session}, {dir} and {bundle} are filled in when they run.

harness.description: The harness's name in Aboard: in ABOARD_SESSION, hook commands and the board file.

name.description: The name people know the harness by.

drives.description: real: this profile runs the tool itself. reimplementation: it runs something that imitates the tool (with its own settings, plugins, hooks or auth), which is a separate harness entry, never presented as the tool.

reimplements.description: For a reimplementation, the harness it imitates.

skills_dir.description: Where aboard init puts the Aboard skill, under the home directory.

interactive.description: Starting an interactive session, for a terminal launcher such as tmux.

start.description: Starts a session with a first prompt.

headless.description: Running one turn without a terminal, for the headless runner. Each turn carries the agent's new messages as its prompt.

via.description: native: the harness's own non-interactive mode, with the commands below. acp: an Agent Client Protocol agent, started with acp.command.

run.description: Runs one turn and prints machine-readable output.

resume.description: Runs one turn in an earlier session.

session_from.description: Where the session id to resume is found in the run's output.

acp.description: The harness's Agent Client Protocol agent, if it has one.

package.description: Where to get the ACP agent.

env.description: Environment for the ACP agent; {command_path} is the harness's own program.

drives.description: Whether the ACP agent runs the real tool or reimplements it.

identity.description: How a session knows which Aboard agent it is.

session.description: How the CLI finds the session it runs in.

launched.description: How a launcher passes the agent's identity to a session it starts, so no join line is pasted.

delivery.description: How the delivery daemon puts messages into a session that is already open.

method.description: stop-hook: a hook waits while the session is idle and wakes it. queue: the harness's own queue takes the bundle. none: the agent runs aboard inbox --wait itself.

queue.description: For queue delivery, the command that queues a bundle.

hooks_file.description: Where aboard init installs the hooks, under the home directory.

event.description: The harness's name for the hook event.

urgent.description: post-tool-hook: urgent messages reach a busy session after its next tool call. idle: they wait for the next idle, first in their bundle.

notes.description: What was learned about the harness that the fields don't say.

json_true.description: A field of the JSON output that must be true; otherwise exit status 0 is enough.
